_comment: Red-flag fast path (SPEC §7.2). Checked before any LLM call. Phrases are matched case-insensitively on word boundaries; a match is ignored when a negation word appears just before it (e.g. 'no chest pain').

flags.label: Chest pain
flags.guidance: Chest pain is a red-flag symptom. Stop all activity now, sit or anchor yourself at rest, and call a crewmate to you. The crew medical officer should start the onboard chest-pain checklist and measure heart rate, blood pressure and SpO2.

flags.label: Difficulty breathing
flags.guidance: Difficulty breathing is a red-flag symptom. Stop all activity, check your SpO2 now, and check the cabin CO2/O2 readings. Call a crewmate to you; the crew medical officer follows the onboard oxygen protocol.

flags.label: Fainting / loss of consciousness
flags.guidance: Fainting is a red-flag symptom. Stay at rest in a secured position and do not move between modules alone. A crewmate should stay with you while the crew medical officer checks heart rate, blood pressure and blood glucose.

flags.label: Coughing, spitting or vomiting blood / uncontrolled bleeding
flags.guidance: Coughing, spitting or vomiting blood, or bleeding that does not stop, is a red-flag symptom. Stop all activity and stay at rest, sitting upright, and call a crewmate to you now. Do not take any medication on your own. The crew medical officer should check heart rate, blood pressure and SpO2 and follow the onboard bleeding checklist; keep any sample (tissue) to show the CMO.

flags.label: Sudden vision loss
flags.guidance: A sudden change in vision is a red-flag symptom. Stop safety-critical tasks now and call a crewmate to you. The crew medical officer should run the onboard vision and neurological checks.

flags.label: Severe headache
flags.guidance: A severe headache is a red-flag symptom. Stop activity and rest at once, and call a crewmate to you. The crew medical officer should check blood pressure and run the onboard neurological checks; also check the cabin CO2 reading.

flags.label: Confusion
flags.guidance: Confusion is a red-flag symptom. Do not continue any task. A crewmate must come to you now; the crew medical officer should check SpO2, blood glucose and temperature and the cabin atmosphere readings.
